messages.content: i made the same meal again today. my brother asked why i do not try something new. i like knowing what i am going to eat.
that is a clear reason. you can enjoy a meal you know without having to choose something new every day.
i do try new food sometimes. i just do not want every dinner to be a new thing to learn.
you could tell him that. choosing a known meal today does not mean you never want a different one.
help me say it without saying his choice to try new food is wrong.
i like that you enjoy trying new food. some days i enjoy that too, but today i wanted a meal i already know i like.
make it shorter and only about my choice.
today i wanted a meal i already know i like.
can i say it was the easiest choice without saying it is the best meal in the world?
yes. the easiest choice for you today is not the same as the best meal for everyone. you could say: this was the easiest choice for me today, and i enjoyed it.
what if he asks what i will make tomorrow?
if you have not chosen, you can say: i do not know yet. i was only talking about today.
thanks. that was what i wanted.
you are welcome. your choice today can stay about today.
write a story about someone choosing a longer way home for a simple reason. do not make the short way wrong.

a student left the library with a book under her arm. she could take the street home in ten minutes, or walk past the park and take longer. she had spent the afternoon sitting and reading, so she chose the walk past the park. she did not need to reach home right away. she wanted to move and look at something other than a page. when she came home, she put the book on the table and felt ready to read again later. the short way would still be there on a busy day.
why did she choose the longer way?
she wanted a walk after sitting and reading all afternoon, and she had enough time for it.
does the story say that longer is always better?
no. the choice worked for her that day. on a busy day, the short way might be more useful.
what fact would change the choice?
if she needed to be home in ten minutes, the longer way might not work. we would need to know how long it took before saying it was possible.
why not just say the longer way takes ten minutes too?
that would change the story. the first way took ten minutes, and the other took longer.
make her explain the choice to a friend.
i have time today, and i want to walk after sitting for so long. i will take the way past the park.
now finish with the short way being useful another day.
the next morning, she needed to reach the library early. she took the short way and was happy to have that choice too.
change i am ready into a question.
am i ready?
now make it a question asking my sister whether she is ready.
are you ready?
why did am become are?
you changed who the question is about. use am with i and are with you in these sentences.
now tell someone that my sister is ready, instead of asking her.
my sister is ready.
can i write my sister are ready?
use my sister is ready. my sister is one person, so is is correct in that sentence.
now ask whether my sister and brother are ready.
are my sister and brother ready?
why not is at the start of that question?
now you are asking about two people together. use are with my sister and brother here.
write all three sentences in order: me, my sister, and both of them.
i am ready. my sister is ready. my sister and brother are ready.
make all three about yesterday.
i was ready yesterday. my sister was ready yesterday. my sister and brother were ready yesterday.
i told my friend that our meeting was at four. i checked the message and it says five. help me fix my answer.
i checked the message again. our meeting is at five, not four. sorry for giving you the wrong time.
should i say the message changed?
only if it really changed. from what you said, you checked it and found a different time from the one you had given. saying the message changed would add a fact you did not give.
write it without saying sorry.
i checked the message again. our meeting is at five, not four. i gave you the wrong time before.
i want to ask them to tell me they saw the change.
you could add: please let me know that you have seen this.
put it all together, but not too long.
the meeting is at five, not four. i gave you the wrong time before. please let me know that you have seen this.
why is saying both four and five useful?
it makes clear which information is wrong and which time to use now. your friend does not have to work out what the change is.
what if i do not know whether five is correct either?
then say you need to check again. do not give five as a sure answer until you know it is the right time.
only give that message now.
i may have given you the wrong time. i will check the message and let you know when i have the correct time.
write a story about two people who both need the table. one wants to read and one wants to draw.

a sister sat at the table with a book open in front of her. her brother came in carrying paper for a drawing. he asked her to move, but she said she was still reading. for a moment, each thought the other wanted the whole table. then their father asked how much space they each needed. the sister moved her book to one side, and the brother put his paper on the other. they both had enough room. later, when he wanted space for a larger picture, he asked when she would finish. she said she would be done soon, so he waited before adding more paper.
why did they think there was a problem at first?
they had not asked how much space each person needed. they thought that using the table had to mean using all of it.
did their first solution work for every part of the day?
no. it worked while the book and drawing each needed a small space. when the brother wanted more space, they had to talk again.
what did he do instead of moving her book himself?
he asked when she would finish and waited for her answer.
write that question in his voice.
when will you be finished reading? i would like more space for my picture.
can the sister say she needs more time?
yes. then they can look for another place to draw or choose a later time. his wish for more space does not make her reading finished.
end with him choosing another place instead.
she said she wanted to read for a while longer. he took his paper to the desk and began there, leaving her book where it was.
i asked where my book was, and someone said it is in the house. that may be true, but i still cannot find it.
you need a more specific place. you could ask: which room is it in, and where in that room should i look?
why is the first answer not enough?
it gives a large area but does not help you choose where to look inside it. an answer can be true and still need more detail for your task.
now they say it is in the bedroom. what should i ask next?
do you know where in the bedroom it is?
what if they only saw it there yesterday?
then they should say that. i saw it in the bedroom yesterday is different from i know it is there now.
write a useful answer from someone who only knows about yesterday.
i saw it on the chair in the bedroom yesterday. i do not know whether it is still there.
why is that better than saying it is on the chair now?
it gives the place they remember while keeping clear what they do not know. you can check the chair without thinking the answer is sure.
now i check and find it on the shelf instead. could the person still have been correct about yesterday?
yes. the book could have been on the chair yesterday and moved later. your finding it on the shelf now does not by itself make their memory false.
give a short thank you without saying they knew the place today.
thank you. looking in the bedroom helped me find it.
